claims.text: Near-equiatomic high-entropy alloy nanoparticles preserve a single solid-solution phase under high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric service conditions.
High configurational entropy kinetically suppresses atomic diffusion.
High configurational entropy suppresses phase segregation.
High configurational entropy suppresses oxidation.
Controlled colloidal synthesis ensures homogeneous nanoparticle size and composition.
Removing one or more elements from a near-equiatomic multielement formulation lowers its configurational entropy.
Temperatures of 773–1173 K are representative of catalytic service, and temperatures of 473–1923 K are representative of thermoelectric service.
Differences in the atomic sizes of constituent elements produce severe lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Severe lattice distortion lowers atomic diffusivity.
Elevated configurational entropy thermodynamically stabilizes a single solid-solution lattice against intermetallic formation and phase segregation.
Entropy-stabilized compositional disorder can stabilize constituent elements in otherwise unfavorable lattice configurations.
The entropy-stabilized lattice retards the atomic mobility required for segregation.
The entropy-stabilized lattice retards the atomic mobility or reactions required for oxidation.
Reduced-complexity nanoparticles have fewer kinetic barriers to atomic rearrangement than the full high-entropy nanoparticles.
Reduced-complexity nanoparticles are more prone to elemental segregation and chemical transformation under identical thermal conditions.
Full high-entropy nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous single-phase structure better than reduced-entropy controls during high-temperature exposure.
Full high-entropy nanoparticles will resist oxidation better than reduced-entropy controls during high-temperature exposure.
Greater retention of structural and chemical homogeneity will preserve catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
The unstressed room-temperature baseline has a well-defined single-phase HEA configuration.
Sufficiently high atomic mobility, strongly oxidizing conditions, or additional reactive species can overwhelm entropy stabilization.
